evidence_items.publisher: International AI Safety Report (chaired by Yoshua Bengio)
evidence_items.locator: section 'Performance remains uneven across tasks and domains'

receipt.public_excerpt: The capabilities of these systems are ‘jagged’: they can perform many complex tasks but still struggle with some seemingly simpler ones. For example, they are less reliable when projects involve many steps; they still sometimes generate text that includes false statements (‘hallucinations’); they are still limited on tasks that involve interacting with or reasoning about the physical world

evidence_items.explanation: An independent international expert review covering frontier AI through November 2025 found that leading systems still failed at some simple tasks and were limited in multi-step work and physical-world reasoning. That is not general human-level ability.

receipt.public_excerpt: ARC Prize 2025 demonstrated continued open-source progress towards AGI, with the top Kaggle score reaching 24% on ARC-AGI-2

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark organisers describe 2025 as 'progress towards AGI', not arrival: the best competition entry scored 24%, far below the 85% Grand Prize threshold. This is one benchmark, under compute limits, so it is supporting rather than decisive.

evidence_items.publisher: Microsoft (8-K exhibit 99.2, via Boardroom Alpha mirror)

receipt.public_excerpt: If Microsoft uses OpenAI’s IP to develop AGI, prior to AGI being declared, the models will be subject to compute thresholds; those thresholds are significantly larger than the size of systems used to train leading models today.

evidence_items.explanation: In late October 2025, Microsoft and OpenAI described AGI as not yet declared and set up an independent panel to verify any future declaration. This shows that the leading lab had made no formal AGI claim by then.

receipt.public_excerpt: “AGI kinda went whooshing by… okay fine, we built AGIs”

evidence_items.explanation: Records an informal December 2025 remark by Altman suggesting AGI had passed. It is a loose, unverified remark, not a demonstrated or verified system, and the same timeline notes he later called a similar claim 'spiritual', not literal. So it does not meet the contradiction condition.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed definition of AGI, so no single source can certify that AGI was absent in 2025.
The original reports of Altman's December 2025 'whooshing by' remark could not be read directly.
